why.MG_geometry_easy.level_up_param: 3.12.1 (owner: Easy has to be simple, Medium harder, Hard harder still): up 6500 → 6000 ({VG, VG, VG} or better). The new Easy pool has no near-copies of the easiest triangles (the near-equilateral one and the right isosceles one were each there twice), and at 6500 the model average player passed 85 % of the games (novice 55 %); at 6000 — 99 % (novice 86 %), 3 games for 3 steps. Scores go in steps of 500, so there is nothing between. Before: Easy asks 93 % of the maximum ({P, P, P} or {P, P, VG}) and is the strictest step: with the doc's noise model (tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs, real figures and comparison, σ = 6 / 4 / 2 % of the field) novice 29 %, average 62 %, strong 98 % (Medium: 13 / 48 / 97 %). up 6500 ({P, VG, VG} or {P, P, G}, 87 % of the maximum like Medium 83 % and Hard 87.5 %): novice 68 %, average 92 % (3 games for 3 steps), strong 100 %; the same with the memory-load variant. Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18 — the average model player opens all 12 games in 23–30 trainings instead of 30–42 (tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py).
why.MG_geometry_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 10000 → 8500 of 12000 (4 figures; Bad 1500, Good 2000, Very Good 2500, Perfect 3000). 10000 asked for Very Good on every figure on average; 8500 is three Good and one Very Good, or one Bad among three Very Good. Novice 12 → 48 %, average 49 → 82 %, strong 97 → 100 % (the memory-load model of tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs; the scores step by 500 and 9000 gives 39 / 78 %). Games for the 5 steps: novice 39 → 10, average 10 → 6. Weak games (< 3400): novice 1 %. Easy stays at 6500 (novice 68 %, average 92 %): it was already inside the new Easy target.
why.MG_geometry_hard.level_up_param: Owner: hard was practically impossible — up 17500 passed 3 % of the games of the model average player with memory load (15 % in the doc's model), 283 games for the 10 steps. With 15 s and the three replaced figures up 16500 (e.g. three Very Good and two Good, or four Very Good and one Bad) gives: average 27 % (doc's model 57 %), strong 97 % (100 %), novice 1 % (5 %); weak games (< 6600): average 1 %, novice 24 %; 36 games for the 10 steps of the average player. The two player models bracket the truth; the fit follows the one with memory load because it reproduces the owner's experience. Mean scores of the average player rise 6865 / 9391 / 14225 (x1.37, x1.51). Easy (6500: average 92 %, novice 68 %) and medium (10000: average 49 %, novice 13 %) stay: scores move in steps of 500, the next easy threshold (7000) would drop the average player to 62 %.
why.geometry_game_field.diff_max_time: Content ladder: easy = 3 triangles, medium = 4 quadrilaterals, hard = 5 figures of 4-11 vertices — and all three give the same 10 s to memorise. Hard gets 15 s (1.4-3.8 s a vertex, like the 2.5-3.3 s of easy and medium). In the player model with memory load (tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs: vertex noise sigma 6 / 4 / 2 % of the field, growing with the vertices per memorising time) the mean hard score of the average player goes 13092 -> 14225 together with the figure changes below.
why.geometry_fig_d2.0_fig: Was a plain rectangle (9,70 9,20 90,20 90,70): the comparison looks at the angles only, so any rectangle is Perfect — a task easier than the medium figures on the hardest level. Replaced by an L-shape of 6 vertices (five right angles and one of 270 deg). Checked with the real comparison: simple polygon, inside the field, vertices at least 25 units apart, an exact copy scores 100 in any rotation, size and drawing order; model average player 3091 of 4000 a round (other hard figures of 4-6 vertices: 3094-3490).
why.geometry_fig_d2.1_fig: Was the second plain rectangle of the hard pool (20,69 20,29 80,29 80,69). Replaced by an arrow-shaped pentagon (angles 90, 141, 77, 142, 90 deg); same checks; model average player 3108 of 4000 a round.
why.geometry_fig_d2.12_fig: Was a near-regular decagon with one notch — the outlier of the pool: the model average player gets Very Bad (0 points) in 78 % of the attempts (24 % in the doc's model without memory load), and at one and the same threshold (16000) a session with this figure passes 7 % of the time, a session without it 33 %; 36 % of the hard score variance of the average player came from the draw of figures. Replaced by a T-shape of 8 vertices (six right angles, two of 270 deg): Very Bad in 26 %, like the 7-8-vertex figures 9_fig, 11_fig and 13_fig (20-25 %); the draw now explains 20 % of the variance. The 11-gon 14_fig stays as the hardest figure (Very Bad in 52 %).

why.geometry_results_data: 3.12.3 (owner: a copy that looks very much like the original gets a number nobody can explain; the logic of the estimate has to be understood and corrected). The number of the original is the share of the tolerance of the level that is left (60 / 30 / 20 % of the angle sum), so one and the same drawing read differently on every level: a hexagon with 63° of angle differences in all was 86 % on Easy, 71 % on Medium and 57 % on Hard. The game now shows 100 minus the sum of the angle differences in percent of the angle sum — one scale for every level (that hexagon: 91 %), and the bands say how strict a level is. The limits are the bands of the original (10 / 25 / 50 / 85 % of the tolerance) moved to the new scale: Bad, Good, Very Good, Perfect start at 46 / 55 / 70 / 91 % on Easy, 73 / 77 / 85 / 95 % on Medium and 82 / 85 / 90 / 97 % on Hard. Easy and Hard are exactly as before; on Medium two limits fell between whole percents (77.5 and 95.5) and were rounded down, in the player's favour. max_fig_diff_miss_percent is no longer read. 3.12.4 (owner: Easy is won often by a beginner, but not every time): Very Good on Easy starts at 78 % instead of 70 %, so the ladder of Very Good is 78 / 85 / 90 %. The step of Easy (6000, three Very Good) passed 87 % of the novice's games (target 60–75 %), and the points go by 500, so the threshold itself could not be set between 6000 and 6500 (6500: novice 55 %, average 85 %). With 78 %: novice 74 %, average 96 %, strong 100 % (memory model of tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs).
